correctness.rationale: For each ordered center and unordered leaf pair, deletion yields a uniform labeled Cayley tree on n-2 vertices; reattachment shifts the total leaf number by exactly two minus the old leaf indicator for the center. Summing marked indicators proves the all-test-function Palm identity. Prüfer word omission gives exact means, decreasing leaf probabilities prove strict positivity, ordered cherry overlap classes give the second moment, and fixed-deletion expansions give both positive asymptotic variance rates and the stated limiting correlation. Exact checker performed 631 assertions for exhaustive n=4..8 and formulas n=9..200; not mistaken for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Classical cherry counts and the marked deletion ingredient appear in Erdős–Rényi (1963) §5 and are acknowledged. The novel asserted content is the mixed global leaf-count Palm distribution, exact covariance sign and persistent correlation, which do not follow as stated from inspected primary results. The ranked coalescent and degree-three-center treatments use different objects/statistics. Bounded result-index queries found no dominating claim, with explicit historical-priority residual risk.
residual_risks: A historical general labeled-forest bivariate enumeration may implicitly imply the Palm identity even without stating it; the inspected papers and bounded searches do not establish global priority.

The exact day of first public release of the 1963 classical source is not independently known; the dated 2011-12-06 preprint is the earliest securely day-dated electronic anchor among the inspected sources.

value.rationale: Local leaf-pair symmetries are natural graph automorphism motifs; global leaf abundance is a distinct canonical tree-shape statistic. An exact size-biased distribution for every test function yields more information than a standalone covariance, while strict all-n positivity and a nonvanishing limiting correlation quantify an enduring local-versus-global shape dependence in the basic uniform labeled tree model.
